hints: The centre of the circle is $(3, -1)$ and radius is $4$.
At $P(3, 3)$, the radius is vertical ($x = 3$), so the tangent is horizontal: $y = 3$.
At $Q(7, -1)$, the radius is horizontal ($y = -1$), so the tangent is vertical: $x = 7$.
walkthrough:
A vertical radius has a horizontal tangent, and conversely.
At $P(3, 3)$, the radius connects $(3, -1)$ to $(3, 3)$ along the vertical line $x = 3$. The tangent is horizontal:
$$\text{Tangent at } P: \quad y = 3$$

At $Q(7, -1)$, the radius connects $(3, -1)$ to $(7, -1)$ along the horizontal line $y = -1$. The tangent is vertical:
$$\text{Tangent at } Q: \quad x = 7$$
